propositions: The parent-first cascade logic is duplicated between claim.py (lines 200-237) and transition.py (lines 421-493), with identical ghost/init preconditions but different edge tables, causing maintenance burden and potential divergence.

The cascade implementation must extract only the shared walk (ancestor recursion, cycle guard, TOCTOU re-check, error rewrap) while keeping _CASCADING_EDGES in transition.py, because the inbound writer already single-sources the decision table.
Three cascading edges exist: (open→in_progress), (closed→open), and (closed→in_progress); a consolidated implementation must preserve all three, not silently drop reopen or reactivation cascades.
The shared cascade must route ConcurrencyMismatch exceptions with exit code 10 preserved, and support injection of resolve_parent and advance callables so each caller retains its own write primitive.
A parametrized test over the live _CASCADING_EDGES table is required to prevent future 'unknown edge' bugs like cranial-sulfur-peafowl and paragonite-fruited-minnow from silently landing.
